key_insight: LongStraw makes million-token RL post-training feasible on a fixed GPU budget by restructuring execution to avoid keeping the full training graph live.
engineering_relevance: It shows how architecture-aware replay and selective state retention can extend RL system scale far beyond standard 256K-token post-training limits.
method: Evaluate the shared prompt without autograd to avoid storing full prompt activations.
Retain only the model-specific state needed for later tokens.
Replay short response branches one at a time to shrink peak memory at the cost of extra compute time.
evidence_signal: On 8 H20 GPUs, LongStraw reaches 2.1M positions for grouped Qwen scoring and backward passes, with only 0.21 GB extra peak memory when increasing group size; a stress test reaches 4.46M positions.
watch_item: The reported runs validate execution capacity, not full training correctness, because captured prompt state is detached and some distributed forward/gradient composition paths are incomplete.
paper_title: LongStraw: Long-Context RL Beyond 2M Tokens under a Fixed GPU Budget
